pages.definition: A shared form of irony where two people bond over a mutual annoyance or absurd situation. Unlike hostile sarcasm, this is used to build rapport by creating an 'us against the world' dynamic.
visualCues: Shared eye contact followed by an eye roll
Relaxed posture indicating lack of genuine threat

scenario.context: Workplace: Two colleagues attempting to use a printer that jams for the third time today.
scenario.description: Both participants are frustrated, but the speaker uses sarcasm to lighten the mood rather than express anger at the listener.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Flat, dry tone with a slight sigh. Emphasis on 'advanced' and 'technology'.

pages.transcript: I am simply in awe of this advanced technology. It keeps us humble.

appropriateResponse.description: A response that matches the dry wit, confirming the shared frustration without fixing the problem immediately.

scenario.context: Social: Two friends arrive at a picnic spot just as it begins to pour rain.
scenario.description: The speaker initiates a shared joke about their bad luck.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Overly enthusiastic voice that drops into a flat tone at the end.

pages.transcript: Honestly, perfect weather. I was actually worried we might get too much sun today.

appropriateResponse.description: Validating the sarcasm by agreeing that the rain is actually 'preferable' in a joking manner.
keyElements: Sarcastic agreement (e.g., 'Yeah, I love being soaked')

scenario.context: Commuting: Two strangers stuck on a train that has been delayed for 20 minutes.
scenario.description: Building temporary solidarity through shared misery.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Slow, dragged out tempo. Deep sigh at the beginning.

pages.transcript: I guess they just wanted to give us some quality time to really appreciate the tunnel walls.

appropriateResponse.description: Participating in the observational humor about the delay.
keyElements: Tone matching the low energy of the situation
